topic.readerProblem: Measure whether an AI citation dataset with many URLs still depends heavily on one or two normalized hosts.
topic.connection: Source concentration adds an inspectable dependency metric to AEOeye-style citation and brand-visibility audits.

assessment: The page provides a populated 30-row synthetic citation dataset, transparent host normalization, HHI, top-source share, and effective-domain calculations. It avoids treating competition-policy thresholds as an AEO quality grade.

sources.supports: The HHI concentration concept, used here only as a descriptive mathematical reference.
URI syntax boundaries for absolute HTTP and HTTPS inputs.
The URL parsing functions used for host extraction.
Provenance context for citation records and collection activities.

checks: Ran all 30 synthetic citation rows and confirmed the generated JSON byte-matches expected-report.json.
Recomputed HHI as 0.206666..., top-one share as 10/30, top-three share as 20/30, and effective domains as 1/HHI.
Changed one temporary URL to ftp:// and confirmed rejection with exit 2; read the final article and opened all sources and artifacts.

artifacts.description: Dependency-free host concentration calculator with explicit URL validation and normalization boundaries.
Populated 30-row synthetic citation fixture across seven normalized hosts.
Deterministic host counts, shares, HHI values, and effective-domain result.
Exact byte-comparison and malformed-URL failure commands with method limits.

methodology: Editorial review executed the normal and malformed-input paths, compared output bytes, independently recalculated each published metric from host counts, opened the four primary sources, and checked all resource and internal links.
limitations: The calculator counts normalized hosts, not registrable domains or owners. It does not follow redirects, infer canonicals, assess support or authority, prove independence, or explain provider selection.
